title: Common-fibre coranks of two finite presentations
statement: Let E be a totally disconnected normed field, X any scheme, P a module over its condensed E coefficient ring, C a pro-etale cover, and f_i:R_i^{m_i} to R_i^{n_i} finite free presentations of the inverse images of P. At v in C_i and w in C_j with the same image in X, n_i minus the rank of the continuous presentation matrix evaluated at v equals n_j minus its rank evaluated at w. No noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Example 3.1; agent rank/descent argument in original node, Common-fibre coranks of two finite presentations

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback to find a point z of C_i times_X C_j above v,w. Take Omega to be an algebraic closure of its residue field. The composite Spec(Omega) to Spec(kappa(z)) to the fibre product followed by either projection gives morphisms a,d with equal composites to X; Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply proves their marked-point images are v,w. This proves the common-geometric-point construction without any new lemma.

Obtain compatible additive finite-colimit-preserving evaluation functors F and G and regular-module linear equivalences from the geometric evaluation theorem. Construct finite-free coordinates with F.mapBiproduct, ModuleCat.biproductIsoPi, and the regular equivalence in each coordinate. Prove the projection formula, then that the inverse sends a standard single-coordinate vector to the image of its biproduct inclusion. Apply LinearMap.toMatrix′ to reduce the entire evaluated finite-free map to its regular-module components; the geometric theorem’s scalar equations identify each component with the canonical continuous presentation matrix evaluated at v or w. Thus the finite-free coordinates and both mulVec equations are proved directly.
Map the two supplied cokernel presentation isomorphisms by F and G. Their comparison on the pullbacks of P identifies the two evaluated cokernels, using PreservesCokernel.iso on both sides.

For each evaluated finite-free map, transport its range by the coordinate linear equivalences and use their mulVec equation to identify its range dimension with the displayed matrix rank. ModuleCat.cokernelIsoRangeQuotient identifies its cokernel with the target modulo that range. Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank and the target coordinate equivalence give n minus matrix rank. Apply finrank invariance to the cokernel isomorphism to conclude.
